player_0.content: New plan: My previous attempt failed because I tracked the state of every player, which introduced unnecessary complexity and increased the risk of a tracking error, even though the final result for Alice happened to be correct in my trace (suggesting the "LOSE" outcome might stem from a subtle logic slip in a similar step or a requirement to be more direct). To ensure accuracy and efficiency, I will adopt a "target-focused" strategy. Instead of updating the full state of all five players, I will track **only** the ball currently held by Alice. I will initialize Alice's ball as "orange" and then iterate through the swap list: if a swap involves Alice, I will update her ball to the color held by her partner (which I must deduce by tracking the partner's ball only when they interact with Alice or by maintaining a minimal map of the two involved parties). If a swap does not involve Alice, I will ignore it entirely. This reduces the cognitive load and minimizes the chance of state corruption. Finally, I will output the option corresponding to the final color held by Alice.
